title: Arctic amplification is caused by sea-ice loss under increasing CO2
problem: The cause of Arctic amplification remains under debate, with the relative importance of proposed mechanisms like sea-ice loss, radiative feedbacks, and poleward energy transport in explaining its strong seasonal and spatial patterns being unclear.
method: To determine the cause of Arctic amplification, the authors analyze historical data and model simulations, including dedicated climate experiments with and without fixed Arctic sea-ice cover, to isolate the impact of sea-ice loss on surface heat fluxes and warming under increasing CO2.
task: This paper's task is to resolve the debate over the cause of Arctic amplification by analyzing observational data and climate model simulations to demonstrate that sea-ice loss is the necessary driver of this phenomenon under increasing CO2.
innovation: This paper provides comprehensive evidence from observations and model experiments to establish that sea-ice loss is the necessary cause of large Arctic amplification, primarily through enhanced cold-season heat and radiation fluxes from newly opened ocean waters.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: Warming in the Arctic has been much faster than the rest of the world in both observations and model simulations, a phenomenon known as the Arctic amplification (AA) whose cause is still under debate.
